verdict: NO-GO -- the multi-task sequence CNN (0.488, 3-seed stable) beats distance (0.393) but underperforms epigenetics-only (0.519) and the TF-identity GBM (0.608). Ship the Tier-1 GBM. The label-shuffle control collapses to 0.081 (~base rate 0.055), so the model is legit (no leak/overfit) -- just not better. 569 positives are too few for a from-scratch CNN to out-predict measured ChIP.
IMPORTANT_scope_caveat: This tested a REDUCED version of the intended multi-task architecture. The auxiliary 311-TF-binding head was trained on ONLY the ~3,961 CRISPR-tested elements, NOT on millions of genome-wide loci. The full design's key mechanism -- pretraining the shared encoder on the whole genome's TF-ChIP labels to SOLVE data starvation, then attaching the sparse CRISPR head -- was NOT implemented. So this NO-GO refutes the data-limited version, NOT the full architecture. The from-scratch CNN was asked to learn the TF combinatorial grammar from ~4,000 sequences, which is exactly the data-starvation the aux-pretraining was meant to avoid but here didn't.
note: Tier-2 multi-task sequence CNN (element DNA -> aux 311-TF-binding head + regulation head on embedding+8 tabular), trained on Colab GPU, chromosome-held-out AUPRC, 3 seeds + label-shuffle control. Real ENCODE K562 CRISPR data. NO-GO FOR THE REDUCED VERSION: 0.488 beats distance (0.393) but underperforms epigenetics-only GBM (0.519) and TF-identity GBM (0.608); shuffle control 0.081 = legit no-leak. Root cause = the aux task was NOT trained on genome-wide loci (see scope caveat), so it couldn't solve data starvation. Production model for now = Tier-1 GBM (TF identity, 0.608). THE REAL TIER-2 TO BUILD: pretrain the shared encoder on ~1-2M genome-wide candidate elements (ENCODE cCREs) with their 311-TF ChIP binding vectors (dense, millions of loci), THEN fine-tune the sparse CRISPR head -- the version actually designed to beat data starvation and the GBM. Alternatively a pretrained foundation model (Enformer/Borzoi) embeddings.
